query: SELECT * FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE database_name='bgp' ORDER BY schema_name,function_name,parameter_types
rows: Number of AS-path prepends (padded repeated ASNs)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the number of AS-path prepends: extra occurrences of an ASN that immediately repeats its predecessor, i.e. an AS padding its own number to deprioritize a route. `[1,1,1,2]` has two prepends, `[1,2,3]` has none. NULL input is NULL.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Count the prepended (padded) ASNs in a path (here 1).","sql":"SELECT bgp.main.as_path_prepends([7018, 174, 174, 13335]);"}]
rows.vgi.title: AS-Path Prepend Count

rows: Parse a standard community 'asn:value' into a STRUCT(asn, value)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Parse a standard BGP community string ('<asn>:<value>') into a `STRUCT(asn UINTEGER, value UINTEGER)`. Returns a NULL struct for anything that is not a plain two-part community — a large community ('a:b:c'), a well-known mnemonic ('NO_EXPORT'), or NULL input. Use it to filter or group routes by community without a regex.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Parse a standard community into (asn, value), e.g. `community_parse('65001:100')` = {asn: 65001, value: 100}.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Split a standard community into {asn: 65001, value: 100}.","sql":"SELECT bgp.main.community_parse('65001:100');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Parse BGP Community

rows: Whether a community string is an RFC 8092 large community

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return whether a community string is a large community (RFC 8092): exactly three colon-separated unsigned-integer parts, '<global>:<data1>:<data2>'. False for a standard 'a:b' community or a well-known mnemonic; NULL input is NULL.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Whether a community is a large community, e.g. `is_large_community('65001:1:2')` = true.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Detect a large community (three numeric parts, so true).","sql":"SELECT bgp.main.is_large_community('65001:1:2');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Large-Community Classifier

rows: The origin AS (last AS) of an AS path

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the origin AS of an AS path — the last (right-most) ASN, which announced the prefix. NULL for an empty or NULL path. Join the result against an RPKI/VRP table to validate route origins (route-origin validation lives in vgi-netflow, not here).
rows.vgi.doc_md: Origin AS of an AS path, e.g. `origin_asn([7018,174,13335])` = 13335.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Get the origin AS that announced the prefix (here 13335).","sql":"SELECT bgp.main.origin_asn([7018, 174, 13335]);"}]
rows.vgi.title: AS Path Origin

rows: Whether an AS path traverses a given ASN

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return whether an AS path traverses a given ASN anywhere along it. NULL if the path is NULL. Use it to find every route that passes through a suspect transit AS (leak detection).
rows.vgi.doc_md: Whether an AS path contains an ASN, e.g. `path_contains([7018,174,13335], 174)` = true.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Test whether a path traverses AS 174 (here true).","sql":"SELECT bgp.main.path_contains([7018, 174, 13335], 174);"}]
rows.vgi.title: AS Path Contains ASN

rows: Number of AS hops in an AS path

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the number of AS hops in an AS path (its length) — the `LIST(UINTEGER)` `as_path` column from read_rib / read_updates. An empty path is 0; NULL input is NULL. Use it to rank routes for leak/hijack triage (a suspiciously long or short path).
rows.vgi.doc_md: Number of AS hops in an AS path, e.g. `path_length([7018,174,13335])` = 3.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Count the AS hops in a path (here 3).","sql":"SELECT bgp.main.path_length([7018, 174, 13335]);"}]
rows.vgi.title: AS Path Length

rows: List the distinct peers / collectors in an MRT file

rows.vgi.doc_llm: List the distinct BGP peers in an MRT file: one row per (peer_ip, peer_asn, collector) triple. For a TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB it returns every peer in the PEER_INDEX_TABLE, with the RIB view name as the `collector`; for a BGP4MP update stream it returns each distinct peer that produced a message, and `collector` is NULL (a raw update stream carries no collector name). Unlike read_rib / read_updates this function never emits an `error` column and takes no `strict` option — a torn or truncated tail simply ends the enumeration. `src` is a path (local, glob, `s3://`, or `http(s)://`) or an inline `BLOB` of MRT bytes; `.gz`/`.bz2` auto-decompress. peer_ip is a DuckDB INET value (cast with `::INET`). Use it to enumerate vantage points before scanning a dump, or to join peer ASNs against attribution data.
rows.vgi.doc_md: List the distinct peers in an MRT file: peer_ip (INET), peer_asn, and collector (the RIB view name for a TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB, NULL for a BGP4MP update stream). `src` is a path / glob / `s3://` / `http(s)://` URL or a `BLOB`; `.gz`/`.bz2` auto-decompress.
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"peer_ip","type":"STRUCT(ip_type UTINYINT, address HUGEINT, mask USMALLINT)","description":"The peer's IP address in DuckDB's INET physical layout; cast `::INET`."},{"name":"peer_asn","type":"UINTEGER","description":"The peer's autonomous-system number."},{"name":"collector","type":"VARCHAR","description":"The RIB view name (TABLE_DUMP_V2 PEER_INDEX_TABLE); NULL for a BGP4MP update stream, which carries no collector name."}]
rows.vgi.title: List MRT Peers / Collectors

rows: Read an MRT TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB snapshot into rows

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Scan an MRT TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB snapshot (a RouteViews / RIPE RIS `rib.*` archive) into one row per (prefix, peer) RIB entry. `src` is a path — local, a glob, an `s3://` URL, or an `http(s)://` URL — or an inline `BLOB` of MRT bytes; gzip (`.gz`) and bzip2 (`.bz2`) inputs are decompressed transparently. Each row carries the route timestamp, RIB view name, the reporting peer (peer_ip INET, peer_asn), the prefix (INET), the AS path (`LIST(UINTEGER)`), origin ASN, next hop (INET), communities (`LIST(VARCHAR)` — standard and large), MED, local pref, atomic-aggregate flag, and aggregator ASN. prefix / peer_ip / next_hop are DuckDB INET values (cast with `::INET`), so prefix containment (`prefix::INET <<= '203.0.113.0/24'`) and joins against vgi-netflow / geoip work without parsing strings. A malformed record yields a row with NULL fields and a populated `error` column unless `strict => true`. This is the RIB counterpart of read_updates.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Scan an MRT TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB dump into rows: timestamp, view_name, peer_ip (INET), peer_asn, prefix (INET), as_path (`LIST(UINTEGER)`), origin_asn, next_hop (INET), communities (`LIST(VARCHAR)`), med, local_pref, atomic_aggregate, aggregator_asn, and an `error` capture column. `src` is a path / glob / `s3://` / `http(s)://` URL or a `BLOB`; `.gz`/`.bz2` auto-decompress. Cast INET columns with `::INET` for containment.

rows: Read an MRT BGP4MP update stream into rows

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Scan an MRT BGP4MP update stream (a RouteViews / RIPE RIS `updates.*` archive) into one row per BGP message: a prefix announcement, a withdrawal, or an FSM state change. `src` is a path — local, a glob, an `s3://` URL, or an `http(s)://` URL — or an inline `BLOB` of MRT bytes; gzip (`.gz`) and bzip2 (`.bz2`) inputs are decompressed transparently. Each row carries the timestamp, the reporting peer (peer_ip INET, peer_asn), the message_type ('announce' / 'withdraw' / 'state_change'), the prefix (INET), AS path (`LIST(UINTEGER)`), origin ASN, next hop (INET), communities (`LIST(VARCHAR)`), and — for state changes — old_state and new_state. prefix / peer_ip / next_hop are DuckDB INET values (cast with `::INET`) so containment and prefix joins work without parsing strings. Announcements and withdrawals stay in one stream so RIB churn can be reconstructed over time. A malformed record yields a row with NULL fields and a populated `error` column unless `strict => true`. This is the update-stream counterpart of read_rib.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Scan an MRT BGP4MP update stream into rows: timestamp, peer_ip (INET), peer_asn, message_type (announce/withdraw/state_change), prefix (INET), as_path (`LIST(UINTEGER)`), origin_asn, next_hop (INET), communities (`LIST(VARCHAR)`), old_state, new_state, and an `error` capture column. `src` is a path / glob / `s3://` / `http(s)://` URL or a `BLOB`; `.gz`/`.bz2` auto-decompress. Cast INET columns with `::INET` for containment.
